title: Serve HTTP before the Engram boot-recovery barrier (per-session readiness gating)
outcome: Greg priority (2026-09-01). Cold start of the live release: termal.exe started 06:23:45, first Codex app-server child 06:24:22 (~37 s). Root cause confirmed at HEAD 18e36dd: src/main.rs:150 runs state.run_post_listen_boot() (review-submission recovery, then the Engram recovery barrier) BEFORE axum::serve at src/main.rs:186, so the listener is bound but no request is served until the whole barrier finishes; warm /api/health median 0.2 ms and /api/state 5.9 ms prove it is the boot barrier, not the state mutex. Required: bind and serve immediately; run boot recovery in the background; gate only the sessions whose recovery is still pending (explicit per-session readiness state visible to the UI, prompts to those sessions wait or fail fast with a clear reason); /api/health and /api/state answer during recovery. Acceptance: cold start to first served /api/state under 1 s on the live machine; sessions with pending recovery carry a readiness marker until done; tests for the readiness gate and for serving during recovery. Related: the app_boot comment that claims a 600 ms boot must be corrected to the real contract. Implementer: Termal::Codex; verification by a different agent (Termal::Fable) per Greg.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 1a, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE. HTTP is served before the recovery barrier, landed in aeaa20b (ancestor of master f7db2c58). Closed by evidence.
